key_insight: CEDAR, an evidence-citing and self-auditing LLM pipeline, outperformed trained machine-learning models in predicting pediatric diabetes outcomes, with the largest gains on sparsely screened outcomes.
engineering_relevance: Evidence citation and self-auditing offer a promising design pattern for making multimodal clinical prediction systems more traceable and reviewable.
method: Combined structured records and note-derived social determinants, plus continuous glucose monitoring data for type 1 diabetes.
Used 18 months of follow-up to predict outcomes at 24 months: seven for type 2 diabetes and four for type 1 diabetes.
Compared predictive performance with trained machine-learning models and assessed cited-value accuracy and clinician agreement.
evidence_signal: Across 2,489 youth with type 2 and 4,018 with type 1 diabetes, pooled AUROC was 0.815 versus 0.656–0.700 and 0.756 versus 0.603–0.631, respectively; only 4 of 70,246 cited values mismatched the chart.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish external or prospective validation; accurate citations and clinician agreement alone do not demonstrate clinical safety.
paper_title: Agentic LLM reasoning in pediatric diabetes outcome prediction from multimodal medical records
